excerpts.text:
# HTTP Methods Explained: GET, POST, PUT, DELETE & More

API Design19 min read
The reality: HTTP methods have precise semantic contracts defined in **RFC 9110** (published June 2022, the current HTTP semantics standard that supersedes RFC 7231).
* ▸**Safe methods** (GET, HEAD, OPTIONS, TRACE) are guaranteed read-only. Caches, crawlers, and prefetch systems call them freely.
* **RFC 9110** (June 2022), "HTTP Semantics." Defines GET, HEAD, POST, PUT, DELETE, CONNECT, OPTIONS, and TRACE. Supersedes RFC 7231.

The safe methods are GET, HEAD, OPTIONS, and TRACE.

The complete idempotent set is therefore **GET, HEAD, OPTIONS, TRACE, PUT, and DELETE**. **POST** and **CONNECT** are not idempotent.

excerpts.text:
RFC 9110 section 9 defines eight methods and classifies each as safe (read only in intent) and idempotent (repeating it has the same intended effect as sending it once):

| Method | Purpose | Safe | Idempotent |
| CONNECT | Establish a tunnel to the server named by the target | no | no |
| TRACE | Message loop back test along the path | yes | yes |
